items.title: What do employers usually look at in hiring?

values: Materials and setup | All are editorially designed fictional material

You are a new apprentice at a repair shop and are only responsible for organizing intake material, marking gaps, and handing off to trained technicians. No contact with real equipment is needed. All models, dates, parts, and personnel are fictional and do not represent manufacturer instructions.

A1 | Intake at 09:00 on 2026-09-16: the customer says "the lawn mower is hard to start and I smelled gasoline"; the equipment card shows model LM-20 and the last four serial digits 4821. The customer provided no purchase date, warranty proof, fuel use history, or repair records. The customer's judgment that "the spark plug is broken" has no test evidence yet.

A2 | Intake photo contents: the housing label LM-20/4821 is legible, and photo F2 shows unidentified fluid traces on the underside of the equipment; the photo has no timestamp or close-up and cannot confirm a fuel leak or judge equipment safety.

A3 | Old record in the work order system: under the same customer name there is equipment number LM-20/4812, whose ignition component was replaced on 2026-07-03. The serial number differs from this 4821, and the old repair cannot automatically be attributed to this machine; the customer and technician must check.

A4 | At 10:00 on 2026-09-16 the customer called hoping to pick up the machine that afternoon and said they would pay a "routine maintenance fee". There is currently no trained technician inspection, quote, parts, warranty status, or safety verification record; completion time and fixed cost must not be promised.

A5 | Responsibility chain: the apprentice records material and marks "pending technician inspection"; the trained technician judges hazards, diagnoses, and verifies per site procedures; the service supervisor checks quotes and customer commitments. If the fluid traces may involve fuel, isolate immediately per the shop safety procedure and notify the responsible person. The system changes status only after the actual evidence is complete and approval is obtained.
Tasks and outputs
List A1—A3 in four categories: equipment identity, customer statements, photo observations, and old records; mark each item's source and credibility limits in the paper matrix.

Use A4—A5 to write follow-up intake questions, items to inspect, stop and escalation conditions, and a customer callback draft; deliver a one-page work order summary containing no diagnostic conclusions.
Reference answer (complete it independently before reading)

A1 shows 4821 and the old order A3 shows 4812, and they cannot be merged. The customer's guess of a spark plug fault has no test evidence; the F2 fluid traces are only a photo observation and cannot characterize a fuel leak or rule out risk.

A4 cannot promise same-day completion or collect a routine maintenance fee, because inspection, quoting, and warranty confirmation have not yet occurred. The trained technician should be notified to check the fluid traces and equipment identity, and the supervisor then decides the reply on the customer's time and price.

Handoff example: work order LM-20/4821, customer description of hard starting and gasoline odor, photo F2 showing unidentified fluid traces, old record with an inconsistent equipment number; status "pending technician inspection, safety issue pending verification", with the responsible person and customer callback to-dos listed.
Boundaries and review

The exercise uses fictional text only and does not start, refuel, disassemble, test, charge, or move real equipment. Photos must not be treated as testing, old orders as the same machine's repair, or customer guesses as faults, and quotes, warranty, or operational verification must not be fabricated. Real risks are handed to trained personnel per site rules.

title.text: Outdoor power equipment and other small engine mechanics

subject.name: Outdoor power equipment and other small engine mechanics
subject.summary: Repair small engines in outdoor power equipment such as lawn mowers, chainsaws, and portable generators: receive the fault description, inspect and diagnose, repair per training and authorization, review, and record labor hours and parts. The site carries fuel, moving parts, and noise hazards; China's agricultural machinery repairer covers only related equipment settings and cannot be directly equated with the US occupation.
